Done. Summary:

- **`out/T3/solution.py`**: loads `inputs/base/model.safetensors`, casts the 64 named projection-matrix patterns to bfloat16, upcasts everything else to float32, drops the 48 buffer patterns, runs the four required checks (64 bf16 tensors, probe tensor is bf16, embed_in is float32, exactly 196 output tensors) before writing, then greedily packs tensors into shards capped at 256 MiB of tensor data (oversized tensors — the two embedding matrices — get their own shard), and writes `model.safetensors.index.json` with the `weight_map`.
- Ran once, succeeded on the first execution: 196 tensors across 9 shards, 48 buffers dropped.
- Verified independently by reopening each shard: the two embedding shards exceed 256 MiB (expected, since they're oversized singleton tensors — and even bigger than the "206 MB" figure in the task because upcasting float16→float32 doubles their size), all other shards are ≤268,435,456 bytes of tensor data.
- Wrote `out/T3/REPORT.md` with the self-report, noting that pitfall about embedding tensor size growth.
